content_list.content_text: In his book Screwball: Hollywood's Madcap Romantic Comedies (1989), Ed Sikov writes that "an entire genre developed around the perverse idea that love could only blossom through misunderstanding".

The genre dominated the screen from 1934 - the year that saw the production of Twentieth Century (1934), It Happened One Night (1934) and The Thin Man (1934) - until 1952, with the last of the classic screwball comedies - Monkey Business (1952) - directed by Howard Hawks (1896-1977). The essential themes of these films - the power of chance, prejudice against the rich and the conflict between romance and economic reality - made moviegoers in the period immediately following the New York stock market crash identify with them.

information.contentText: With Bringing Up Baby, Howard Hawks perfected the screwball comedy. It has all the elements of the genre: the respectable, straitlaced citizen, set against a free spirit of the opposite sex, played by Katharine Hepburn. Although the film was a flop at the time, it has long been recognized as one of the high points of 1930s Hollywood comedy.

content_list.content_text: Screwball comedies can incorporate elements of other genres, such as detective films (The Thin Man), gangster films in Ball of Fire (1941) and black comedy in Arsenic and Old Lace (1944). They can mix humor with stories of economic survival, as in The Palm Beach Story (1942), or dissect populist politics, as in Mr. Smith Goes to Washington (1939). They can be merciless and cynical, as seen in Nothing Sacred (1937), or relatively well-behaved, as in The Philadelphia Story (1940).

quote.quote: When a man is facing a leopard in the middle of a lake, he's in no position to run away.
quote.author: Dr. David Huxley (Cary Grant) in Bringing Up Baby

content_list.content_text: Twentieth Century, based on a Broadway hit by Ben Hecht and Charles MacArthur and directed by Hawks, provides one of the templates for the screwball comedy. Irreverent, acerbic and frenetic, the film stars John Barrymore (1882-1942) as a monstrously egotistical Broadway producer who tries to manipulate his former protégée, played by Carole Lombard (1908-1942), into signing with him once again during a transcontinental train journey. The climax points more to the restoration of a creative hostility between the two than to a romantic resolution.

information.contentTitle: Scene from It Happened One Night (1934)
information.contentText: Clark Gable gives Claudette Colbert a lesson in hitchhiking in It Happened One Night, by Frank Capra. The mismatched couple is one of the most typical devices of the genre.

content_list.content_text: Colliding egos are also present in Hawks's His Girl Friday (1940), a version of Hecht and MacArthur's play The Front Page (1928), which uses a similar narrative line. In the play, an editor tries to lure his best reporter back to work for him. In Hawks's version, Hildy Johnson becomes a female reporter, which adds sexual tension to the professional conflict. Screwball comedy often takes the form of an unsentimental education. In It Happened One Night (1934), directed by Frank Capra (1897-1991), Claudette Colbert's spoiled heiress learns about life and about her own feelings from Clark Gable's gruff journalist.

In My Man Godfrey (1936), by Gregory La Cava (1892-1952), William Powell plays a bum hired by Carole Lombard's scatterbrained socialite as the family butler. She falls in love with him, and he saves her father's business from bankruptcy. The fact that Godfrey is actually a blue blood living in the gutter by choice blunts any claim to social criticism.

information.contentText: The success of The Lady Eve, Preston Sturges's third film for Paramount, established his reputation as the best of the comedy writer-directors in the United States.

content_list.content_text: In The Philadelphia Story (1940), directed by George Cukor (1899-1983), Cary Grant helps his ex-wife Katharine Hepburn understand the limits of her own perfectionism. Hepburn's free and eccentric spirit makes Grant's insecure paleontologist abandon his absurdly cautious existence in the exemplary Bringing Up Baby (1938). Barbara Stanwyck's brazen con artist plans to fleece a rich, shy reptile expert (Henry Fonda) in The Lady Eve (1941), and then teach him a lesson.

Capra's films, however, are exceptions to the rule. For the most part, screwball comedies dispense with lessons on democracy and social engagement. The deepest message of any film in the genre comes in the form of an elegant demonstration of the true nature of the comic muse in Ninotchka (1939), directed by Ernst Lubitsch (1892-1947). Sitting in a café with Garbo's stern Soviet envoy, Melvyn Douglas's bon vivant tries to amuse her with a series of tedious jokes. Discouraged by the beauty's coldness, Douglas leans back in his chair, which breaks and sends him sprawling to the floor - and suddenly Garbo bursts into the most angelic laughter.

movies.title: Bringing Up Baby
movies.overview: David Huxley is waiting to get a bone he needs for his museum collection. Through a series of strange circumstances, he meets Susan Vance, and the duo have a series of misadventures which include a leopard called Baby.

movies.title: It Happened One Night
movies.overview: A renegade reporter and a crazy young heiress meet on a bus heading for New York, and end up stuck with each other when the bus leaves them behind at one of the stops.

movies.title: The Philadelphia Story
movies.overview: When a rich woman's ex-husband and a tabloid-type reporter turn up just before her planned remarriage, she begins to learn the truth about herself.

movies.title: The Lady Eve
movies.overview: It's no accident when wealthy Charles falls for Jean. Jean is a con artist with her sights set on Charles' fortune. Matters complicate when Jean starts falling for her mark. When Charles suspects Jean is a gold digger, he dumps her. Jean, fixated on revenge and still pining for the millionaire, devises a plan to get back in Charles' life. With love and payback on her mind, she re-introduces herself to Charles, this time as an aristocrat named Lady Eve Sidwich.

movies.title: Mr. Smith Goes to Washington
movies.overview: Naive and idealistic Jefferson Smith, leader of the Boy Rangers, is appointed to the United States Senate by the puppet governor of his state. He soon discovers, upon going to Washington, many shortcomings of the political process as his earnest goal of a national boys' camp leads to a conflict with the state political boss.

movies.title: Mr. Deeds Goes to Town
movies.overview: Longfellow Deeds lives in a small town, leading a small town kind of life. When a relative dies and leaves Deeds a fortune, Longfellow moves to the big city where he becomes an instant target for everyone. Deeds outwits them all until Babe Bennett comes along. When small-town boy meets big-city girl anything can, and does, happen.
